records.name: Great Careers Network (Philadelphia Area Great Careers Group)
records.summary: A nonprofit career support group for job seekers in the Philadelphia area. It holds expert panels, skill workshops and peer meetups, and publishes free career resources.
records.what_you_do: Join a free online job seeker session or networking meetup, come to an in-person event in Paoli, or read the free newsletter. Some events ask for a paid membership.

schedule.text: Events are listed on the events calendar. Most are online, and a few are in person at a venue in Paoli. Times vary by event.

locations.label: Main office
locations.address: 53 Darby Road, Suite F, Paoli, PA 19301

cost.text: Some events are free and open to anyone, and the newsletter is free. The events page says RSVP access is limited to paid members. Paid plans are $17 a month, $37 a quarter, or $97 a year.

first_step.how: Pick a free online session on the events calendar and sign up through its Get Tickets button, or subscribe to the free newsletter first.
first_step.basis: Free online sessions and the newsletter are open to anyone, but some RSVPs need a paid membership and the page does not describe a beginner program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most listed sessions last one hour. They bring together people who are looking for work, with talks, job search accountability time and networking. Listed times are in Eastern time.
first_visit_tips: Check the listing for a Get Tickets button or an outside registration link, since some events use a separate sign-up page.
Register early for events with limited tickets.
In-person events are in Paoli, so plan transit or a drive ahead of time.

records.notes: Verdict call for the reviewer: the office and all in-person events are in Paoli (Chester County), not Philadelphia. The group uses the Philadelphia Area name, most of its events are online and open to anyone, so it is published with online_ok true. out_of_area is the alternative. Membership wording differs between pages: the homepage says the free tier includes free networking meetings, while the events page says RSVP access is limited to paid members. Prices are as listed on the membership page and match the events page. The membership page has a confusing quarterly plan title; the record uses the prices only. The site gives no detail on what a peer meetup is like.

records.name: Greater Philadelphia Search and Rescue (GPSAR)
records.summary: A volunteer group that searches for missing people across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Delaware. Its searches are free for families, and its volunteers train in search skills and stay on call around the clock.
records.what_you_do: Search teams, land navigation, logistics, search planning, and communications. Members train in search skills and help run searches once they are dispatched.

schedule.text: On call 24 hours a day, 7 days a week for dispatch. No regular meeting schedule is published.

cost.text: Searches are free to the families they help, though the group asks for donations to cover its work.

first_step.how: Call 877-598-5618 or email chief@gpsar.org, the membership chair, to start the volunteer process.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page sends people to the membership chair before anything else, the application questions it mentions do not appear on the page, and the group calls this a serious commitment, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a serious commitment. Searches can mean late-night call-outs and long days of tiring field work. New members learn search skills, land navigation and logistics, and join real searches once they are dispatched.
first_visit_tips: Read the volunteer page first, since the group asks people to apply only if they can fully commit.
Plan for late-evening call-outs before you apply.

records.notes: Phone and email conflict: the volunteer page gives 877-598-5618 and chief@gpsar.org (membership chair), while the general line is 877-255-5678 and gpsar@gpsar.org. Both are kept, and first_step uses the volunteer line. Tier 1 said the application questions were on the volunteer page; a re-read found no questions or form there, so the record no longer says so. The homepage shows a dispatch entry dated 2026-10-08, but it is a Montco Dispatch traffic feed, not a GPSAR post, so it is not used as evidence. The /faq page returned 404. No training or application steps are published.

records.name: Group Motion Multi Media Dance Theater
records.summary: A dance and movement group that runs open Friday night workshops, retreats and projects. Dancers and non-dancers are both welcome, and the mailing list announces new workshops.
records.what_you_do: Join a Friday night movement workshop with no dance experience needed, or sign up for the mailing list to hear about new workshops and projects.

schedule.text: Friday night workshops are listed one at a time on the Friday Night Workshops page, usually on Friday evenings. Some are on Zoom and some are in person in Philadelphia.

cost.text: Workshops are $25 each, or $20 for students and seniors. Class cards cost less per workshop. Pay through the PayPal link on the site or in cash in person.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list, which gives you the Zoom link for online sessions, then sign up for an upcoming Friday Night Workshop and pay through the PayPal link.
first_step.basis: The site says no dance or movement experience is needed and all are welcome, and it spells out how to sign up. Drop-in is not stated.
first_step.what_to_expect: A workshop starts with a short guided meditation, then moves into movement you do on your own, then group movement and creative exchange. Some sessions have live improvised music. Masks are optional.
first_visit_tips: Wear clothes you can move in.
For a Zoom session, join the mailing list first so you get the link.
For an in-person workshop, pay ahead by PayPal or bring cash.

records.notes: Workshop listings show month and day with no year, so no year is written and no dated evidence is added; status stays probably_active on the working site. The retreats page lists three past retreats (Arizona, Florida, West Virginia) with no years and no sign-up steps, so retreats are not in the record. Sign-up is per workshop, so commitment is one_off. Drop-in is not stated. The newcomer score of 4 rests on the no experience needed line. Friday workshops have no listed end times.

records.name: Habitat for Humanity Philadelphia
records.summary: A housing nonprofit that builds and repairs homes with volunteers across Philadelphia and runs the ReStore. Individuals and groups can volunteer, and the page says all volunteers are welcome.
records.what_you_do: Build or repair homes on a full-day build shift, sort and stock donations at the ReStore, help in the warehouse, or join the Young Professionals volunteer network. Start with a GivePulse account and the virtual orientation.

schedule.text: Build days run Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 3:30 pm, as full-day shifts. ReStore volunteer shifts run 10 am to 1 pm or 1 pm to 4 pm, Monday through Sunday.

cost.text: No volunteer fee is mentioned on the site. Bring your own food and water on build days; Habitat provides tools and safety gear.

requirements.gear: Sturdy closed-toe shoes. Habitat provides hard hats, safety glasses, earplugs and dust masks on build days.

first_step.how: Create a GivePulse account, complete the required virtual orientation for new volunteers, then book a volunteer day in GivePulse.
first_step.basis: The current individuals page lays out the steps, the FAQ says no construction experience is needed because training is on site, and the site welcomes all volunteers.
first_step.what_to_expect: A build day runs 8:30 am to 3:30 pm, with a safety orientation at 8:30 am, so plan on the full day. You do not need construction experience, and training happens on site. Your task is set when you arrive, because the work depends on the stage of the house, and it can range from demolition to landscaping.
first_visit_tips: Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes and clothes you do not mind getting dirty.
Bring your own water and lunch. The lunch break is one hour.
Volunteers aged 16 and 17 cannot use power tools or work more than 10 feet off the ground.

records.notes: Two processes appear. Older Habitat event pages found by search describe a New Volunteer Inquiry form and an in-person ReStore orientation; the current individuals page describes GivePulse and a virtual orientation, so the record follows the current page. Confirm with the volunteer manager. kids_ok is false because the minimum age is 16; the FAQ does not address children. The page says the volunteer manager handles service hours, but no service-hours letter is stated, so it stays unknown. No parking, transit or accessibility details were published. ReStore phone 215-739-9300 is on the individuals page. Pope Leo Village has no sign-up steps and is listed under leads_only. The /individual-volunteering/ URL returned 404.

records.name: Head of the Schuylkill Regatta Volunteers
records.summary: The volunteer crew behind Philadelphia's Head of the Schuylkill Regatta, a rowing race on the Schuylkill River that has run for more than 56 years. Volunteers help with timing, docks, registration, parking and more.
records.what_you_do: Work half day shifts around lunchtime in one of about a dozen roles: timing, docks, registration, parking, hospitality, information, awards, golf carts, logistics, photography, zero waste and boat launches. Timing needs no rowing or timing experience, and training is provided.

schedule.text: Shifts run in half days split around lunchtime on regatta weekend each fall. Most area prep meetings are held on Zoom.

locations.label: Schuylkill River regatta course, near Boathouse Row

cost.text: No fee is listed for volunteers.

first_step.how: Sign up for a shift on the SignUpGenius form linked from the volunteer page, then a Captain confirms your shift and where to report. New volunteers can also attend the all-area volunteer information session on Zoom on Tuesday, October 20, 2026; it is recorded for anyone who misses it.
first_step.basis: The page welcomes new volunteers, says timing needs no rowing experience, provides training, and gives clear steps to start: a shift sign-up and an email contact.
first_step.what_to_expect: A shift lasts about half a day and is split around lunchtime. The work takes place around the regatta course, and the docks role is hands-on. Timing volunteers get training. No fee is listed.
first_visit_tips: Ask volunteers@hosr.org how volunteers get to the course. On race day only vehicles with an HOSR vehicle ID tag can drive onto Kelly Drive, and other traffic uses paid off-site lots with shuttle buses.

Learn where to report misconduct, which the page asks every volunteer to know. Adult volunteers who will not work with minor athletes are encouraged to take the U.S. Center for SafeSport's brief course.
Launch roles need boating experience, and golf cart drivers must be 18 with a driver's license.

records.notes: The venue and parking page (hosr.org/venue-parking/) returned 404, so no SEPTA line or stop is named and access.notes is omitted. The /faq page is the competitor FAQ; only its race-day traffic rule is used, and it is written for spectators and competitors, so the volunteer parking plan should be confirmed by email. Tier 1 had the October 20 information session in schedule text and days [tue]; it is a one time event, so it moved to first_step and days were removed. last_sign_of_life 2026-10 comes from the October 24 and 25, 2026 regatta dates on the homepage. The volunteer page does not say what to wear or where shifts check in. The minimum age of 18 applies only to golf cart drivers, so audience.min_age is omitted.

records.name: Heyday Athletic
records.summary: A company that runs adult sports leagues in the Philadelphia area, including basketball, soccer, kickball, softball, pickleball and tennis. You can sign up alone, with friends, or as a full team, and solo players are placed on balanced teams.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a league alone, with friends, or as a team, then play organized games. The site also lists pickup games, tournaments and social events.

schedule.text: Adult leagues run in seasons, and the site has a sign-up button for its winter league. League nights and season dates are not stated on the site.

cost.text: Price is not stated on the site, and fees are taken at sign-up. An older press roundup (December 2022) listed $50 to $100 to join, so check the current fee before you register.

first_step.how: Use the League Finder to pick a league, open its League Details page, and choose Individual. Sign in, sign the waivers, and pay. Staff then place you on a balanced team.
first_step.basis: Anyone can sign up online with no approval step listed, and solo players are placed on teams. The site describes no beginner division and no first-visit welcome, so it does not rate higher.
first_step.what_to_expect: You pay and sign waivers online, then staff place you on a team by skill, position and player size. Team captains collect payments from their players. The site does not describe the first game night or the venue, so ask through the Contact page before you pay.
first_visit_tips: Choose the group of friends option if you want to be placed with people you know.
Have your payment details and any coupon or gift card ready before checkout.
Ask about the first game night and the venue before you pay, because the site does not list them.

records.notes: Judgement call for the reviewer: Heyday is a for-profit league operator with paid sign-up. It is published because its adult leagues are open to the public, but confirm it fits the rule on businesses with no community program. The Philadelphia page lists sports but no venues, league nights or season dates, and the Locations page returned 404. Listed events (mid October through November 2026, including a volleyball tournament and a golf classic) are one time events, so they are not in schedule text. No email or phone is listed; the Contact page is the way in. Volleyball is offered but has no matching tag in the vocabulary, so it is not tagged.

records.name: Historic Fair Hill
records.summary: A North Philadelphia community organization that cares for the Fair Hill burial ground, a historic Quaker site that holds the graves of abolitionists and early women's rights leaders. It also runs reading, garden, and tree-planting programs and community events.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as a reading buddy, school library helper, garden helper, or tree planter, help with events, or join the Fairhill Neighbors group. Drop in on a Saturday afternoon for Family Fun Saturdays.

schedule.text: Family Fun Saturdays run each Saturday afternoon from April to November. Garden volunteers help on Saturdays from 10 am to 3 pm, Community Clean Up Days are on the third Saturday of the month, and Fairhill Neighbors meets on Zoom on the first Monday, 5 to 6 pm.

cost.text: No cost is listed for volunteering or for Family Fun Saturdays. Produce from Historic Fair Hill's market stalls is always free, and donations are accepted through a PayPal link.

first_step.how: Email info@historicfairhill.com or call (215) 844-1683 ext 107 about a volunteer role, or drop in on a Saturday afternoon for Family Fun Saturdays.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page gives a contact and a next step for each role, Reading Buddies get training, and the Saturday family event is an open invitation with no sign-up listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Family Fun Saturdays are afternoon activities with storytimes, games, arts and crafts, gardening and scavenger hunts. Reading Buddies work one on one with students in a classroom, get training and guidance, and receive help with state clearances and carpools. Some roles need background clearances or training before you start.
first_visit_tips: For an easy first visit, come to a Saturday afternoon Family Fun Saturday and wear clothes you can garden in.
For a volunteer role, email or call first, since some roles need clearances or training before you begin.
The site does not list transit or parking, so ask before you go.

records.notes: Year check: on re-read the homepage shows 2026 for the Family Fun Saturdays start date (April 4), the Open Fire cooking class (October 17, 2026) and the 19133 Farmer's Market (October 30, 2026). The November 21 end date has no year, so the season text does not state one. Tier 1 had said no years were shown; that was corrected. last_sign_of_life moved from 2026-08 (tier 1) to 2026-10 for these listed events. background_check is not set: the page says some roles need clearances and that Reading Buddies get help with state clearances, but it does not name clearances as required for that role. Nearest SEPTA stop is not stated, so access.notes is omitted. Tier 1 called the program Family Fun Days in one place; the homepage name Family Fun Saturdays is used. The volunteer page mentions a weekly farm stand and an annual reading festival, which are not in the record as one time items. The Fairhill Tree Tenders group is named on the volunteer page and listed under leads_only.

notes: Budget: 1 WebSearch (cap 1), used to find Habitat's individuals page. 26 WebFetch calls, within 6 per group. Four URLs returned HTTP 404 and none were blocked: gpsar.org/faq, habitatphiladelphia.org/individual-volunteering/, hosr.org/venue-parking/, and the heyday locations page. No rate limiting seen. Corrections to tier 1: Great Careers verdict is a judgement call (published with online_ok, Paoli office); GPSAR application questions are not on the volunteer page and its contact line differs; Habitat sign-up is now GivePulse plus a virtual orientation; HOSR information session moved out of schedule text; Historic Fair Hill 2026 years confirmed on re-read; Heyday kept as publish but it is a for-profit league operator, so the reviewer should confirm it fits the business rule. Leads with their own websites that were dropped with reasons, not fetched: hopefulfridays.org (host of one listed session on the Great Careers events page, not a group in this batch) and christchurchshorthills.org (registration page for one event). Partner venues (Goodness Bowls, Village of Arts and Humanities, Community Education Center, Summit Presbyterian Church) are places, not groups, and are not listed as leads.
